metadata.title: HITEC near-field benchmark - COx claystone, isotropic, hydro-mechanical excavation + 6-month waiting phase
metadata.validation_method: Digitized pore-pressure and radial-displacement histories at P1-P4, Fig. 7, early segment (0-183.6 d)
metadata.validation_target: Radial convergence at P1 reaching 2.749-2.758 m/1000 at t=183.6 d (all seven teams; closed form 0.95*sigma0*a/(2G) = 2.757 mm) and the p drawdown at P2/P3 during the waiting phase, with P4 undisturbed
metadata.notes:
(1) EXCESS formulation - p and stress are measured from the equilibrated in-situ state (p0 = 4.7 MPa, sigma0 = 12.5 MPa); far-field boundaries are excess-traction-free and excess-p = 0, which exactly reproduces the paper's constant far-field conditions. (2) Both 24 h ramps of paper Table 3 - the stress release to 5% of in-situ and the wall drainage P0 -> Patm - are absolute time_tables. The earlier 'step deconfinement, no piecewise time_function available' workaround is gone. (3) Gallery wall is an 8-chord polygon because Neumann tractions need global components on straight edges (skill BC table). (4) Heating phase NOT included: thermal pressurization needs the u-p-T coupling this backend lacks, so this benchmark stops at the end of the waiting phase (183.6 d).
RESOLVED 2026-08-16 (was: 'OPEN DEFECT - drawdown penetrates only ~0.27 m, ur(P1) 2.12 of 2.757 mm'). Two independent causes, neither of them the upquad11 inf-sup condition the note suspected:
 (a) THE TIME GRID NEVER REACHED OOFEM. builder/physics/hydro_mechanical.make_engine passed BOTH deltaT and prescribedTimes to mpmProblem, but MPMProblem::initializeFrom (src/mpm/mpmproblem.C) reads them as an if/else-if chain with deltat FIRST - unlike transientTransport and staticStructural, which read prescribedTimes first. prescribedTimes was silently dropped and the solver stepped at a constant dt = grid.step_dt(1) = 482.14 s, so 140 steps covered 67500 s = 0.78 d while the DB and the plots were labelled up to 183.6 d. Signature of the bug: every result is EXACTLY linear in the step index (p_P1 = -25669.542 Pa x step to 12 digits). Fixed in the builder: deltaT is now only passed when prescribedTimes is empty.
 (b) dt WAS BELOW THE u-p MONOTONICITY FLOOR. upquad11 is equal-order and unstabilized, so a step is only monotone for dt >= h^2/(6c); with c = 1.35e-7 m2/s and the old 0.1 m wall mesh that floor is 12337 s, against a dt_min of 600 s. The drawdown front rang and the excess pressure overshot POSITIVE a few elements out, which is what made P3 read more drawdown than P2. Fixed by 0.04 m at the wall + dt_min 3600 s (see geometry.mesh.refinement._comment_stability).
VALIDATED after both fixes (114/114 steps, 1465 nodes, 107 s): p(P1) reaches Patm = 0.100 MPa at t = 1.16 d and holds; ur(P1) = 2.738 mm vs the teams' 2.749-2.758 and the closed form 0.95*sigma0*a/(2G) = 2.757 mm (-0.6%); p(r) at t_end is monotone with max positive excess +3.1 kPa (0.07%). Sampled at the TRUE probe radii the run sits INSIDE the seven-team band at every point: ur = 2.738/1.975/1.604/0.724 mm and p = 0.100/1.849/2.923/4.673 MPa at P1-P4.
REMAINING ERROR SOURCE - probe snapping (ANALYSIS.md PROBLEM 4, still open): geometry.points snaps to the nearest EXISTING node and P2/P3/P4 land at r = 1.830/2.444/6.448 instead of 1.9/2.5/6.25. Because ur ~ 1/r that alone accounts for the whole residual in the query columns (+3.1%/+3.0%/-5.0% vs the band-centre, all in the direction of the offset). NOT fixable in this JSON: gmsh_backend._embed_measurement_points returns early when the model has no 3D volume, so a 2D benchmark gets no forced nodes; a dim-0 physical group cannot help either because no CAD vertex exists at those coordinates. Fix belongs in the mesh generator (embed into the containing CURVE - all four probes lie on the sym_bottom edge).

mesh._comment: recombine=true MANDATORY: hydro_mechanical runs on quads only (upquad11), plane strain, unit depth. element_size is the FAR-FIELD size; the near field comes from mesh.refinement.

refinement._comment: 0.04 m at the gallery wall grading to 4 m by r=20 m. Sized from the physics: hydraulic diffusion length sqrt(c_v*t_end) = 1.46 m, so the pore-pressure field lives inside ~2 m; the elastic stress perturbation is (a/r)^2 = 0.4% at r=20 m. A UNIFORM mesh fine enough for the wall would refine 100x100 m of far field that never changes.
refinement._comment_stability: h IS COUPLED TO dt. upquad11 is an equal-order u-p element with no stabilization, so a consolidation step is only monotone for dt >= h^2/(6c); below that the drawdown front rings and the excess pressure OVERSHOOTS TO POSITIVE a few elements out (measured 2026-08-15: p(r) = -3.59e6, -5.3e5, +8.9e4, +9.1e4, -3.9e4 ... which is why P3 showed MORE drawdown than P2). With c = (k/mu)/S = 2.3e-17/1.70e-10 = 1.35e-7 m2/s: h=0.1 needs dt >= 12337 s (too coarse to resolve the 24 h ramps), h=0.04 needs dt >= 1974 s, which the first dt_strategy segment (dt_min 3600 -> 3364 s after normalization) clears with 70% margin. Do not lower this without also raising time_stepping.dt_strategy.segments[0].

pore_pressure._comment_perm: PAPER_VALUE Tab. 1: K = 2.3e-20 m2; named route so the pipeline converts to mobility (never feed m2 into 'mobility' directly)
pore_pressure._comment_Ks: INFERRED: b = 1 - K_d/K_s with K_d = E/(3(1-2nu)) = 5.83e9 -> K_s = 2.92e10 Pa; gives 1/Q = n/K_f + (b-n)/K_s = 1.02e-10 1/Pa

initial_conditions._comment: Excess over the p0 = 4.7 MPa datum. Zero IC + BC-driven field avoids the inadmissible uniform-p/zero-u state (skill trap).

boundary_conditions._comment: EXCESS pressure datum: far field held at p0 = 4.7 MPa absolute = 0 excess (PAPER_VALUE Tab. 3)

PAPER_VALUE Table 3: the wall drains from P0 to Patm (0.1 MPa) IN 24 H, i.e. 0 -> -4.6 MPa excess. Now a time_table -- dirichlet takes absolute time_tables, so the old 'applied as a step because no piecewise time_function exists' workaround is obsolete.
Split across the 8 chord groups: one 'gallery_wall' group covered the SAME curves, and a mesh element carries ONE physical tag in MSH 2.2 -- overlapping groups silently lose the later one.

EXCAVATION STRESS RELEASE, paper Table 3: the wall traction goes from 100% to 5% OF THE IN-SITU STRESS over 24 h, then holds. In this EXCESS formulation that is an applied excess traction of 0 -> -0.95*sigma0*n (sigma0 = 12.5 MPa), i.e. the table below. CONFIRMED against the paper 2026-08-14: 5% is the COx/OPA value, 50% is Boom Clay only.
The table used to run BACKWARDS (full release at t=0 decaying to 5% OF THE RELEASE at 24 h). That inverted the physics -- convergence PEAKED at excavation and decayed, where the paper (p.1634) and all seven teams show it rising throughout the waiting phase -- and left the final load 20x too small. Closed form for the isotropic hole, 0.95*sigma0*a/(2G) = 2.757 mm, matches the teams' 2.749-2.758 mm; do not let this table regress.

time_stepping._comment: transient is mandatory for hydro_mechanical - consolidation IS the time evolution

segments._comment: excavation day; resolves both 24 h ramps. Hydraulic diffusivity c ~ 1.35e-7 m2/s -> 6-month drainage length ~1.5 m: drawdown reaches P2/P3 but not P4, matching the paper. dt_min is NOT free: it is bounded BELOW by the u-p monotonicity floor h^2/(6c) = 1974 s for the 0.04 m wall mesh (see geometry.mesh.refinement._comment_stability). The old 600 s was 20x under that floor and produced positive excess pressure a few elements off the wall. Normalized dt here: 3364 -> 10093 s, 14 steps.

time_stepping._comment_linear_solver: 46378 nodes x 3 DOF ~ 139k unknowns on an unstructured gmsh mesh: skyline is bandwidth-bound and unusable here (107 s/step measured on a 11.6k-unknown mesh). DSS reorders internally. Safe: this model is externally loaded, not the free/unloaded case where DSS's accuracy floor shows.

reference_curves.label: P1 ANDRA COMSOL
reference_curves._comment:
Fig. 7 (p.1634), read from the figure's VECTOR geometry with tools/extract, not digitised: 7 teams x 4 points x 2 quantities = 56 files under reference/PW and reference/UR. One file per entry -- the loader has no glob or file-list form.
SAMPLING WARNING: the pore-pressure panel of Fig. 7 uses a LINEAR 0-3500 d axis, so this benchmark's whole 0-183.6 d window is ~5% of its width -- PW/P1 has only 7 of 84 samples in range. The radial-displacement panel is LOG time (39 of 47 in range). Validate against UR; treat PW as indicative, PW/P1 especially.

queries.label: excess p at P1 [Pa]
queries._comment: P1-P4 all sit on y=0, so the radial direction is +x and ur = -ux exactly -- the paper's sign convention is positive toward the gallery.

plots.name: pw_P1
plots.title: HITEC COx isotropic HM - pore pressure at P1 (gallery wall, r = 1.25 m)
plots._comment:
One plot per point per quantity: 8 lines is the documented ceiling for a line chart. Colour identifies the TEAM and is the same mapping the cox-isotropic-temperature benchmark uses.
xlim is MANDATORY on every plot here: the reference curves run to 3500 d (the paper's full THM run) while this benchmark stops at 183.625 d, so without it the entire comparison window is a 5%-wide sliver at the left edge. ur uses a LOG time axis, as Fig. 7's own displacement panel does - the excavation day and the 6-month waiting phase are three decades apart and a linear axis hides the first.
